acceptance_condition: A structured extraction covering both files with at least 8 distinct findings, each tied to file path + PDF page marker, explicitly labeled as reported finding vs. the extractor's cross-paper inference, and a list of any stated moderators of the debate effect.
rationale: These two papers are the core positive/conditional evidence that multi-agent communication helps; their exact claims, moderators, and baselines are the raw material for reconciling the corpus (D4) and for formulating the mechanism (D2) and task-topology predictions.
text: Extract from papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt and papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt: (a) every reported empirical claim about when multi-agent debate or communication improves accuracy/factuality over single-agent or independent-sampling baselines, with the task, model, number of agents/rounds, and any compute or cost accounting; (b) every reported condition or moderator under which debate fails, degrades, or does not help (task type, answer aggregation rule, model heterogeneity); (c) whether either paper compares against a matched-inference-compute baseline or an open shared transcript, and exactly what they say about it. Record each finding with the workspace file path and the explicit `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker where it appears, and flag findings that appear to conflict across the two papers.
